| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ὣς φάτ’ ἐποτρύνων (20.364, 20.373; whole-line opening, "ὣς φάτο" + ἐποτρύνων "urging on") | "So he spoke, urging them on" | "So he spoke, urging them on" | "So he spoke, encouraging", "exhorting"; follows the table's ἐποτρύνων "urging on" and ὣς φάτο "So he spoke" |
| ἀλεξητήρ (ἐσθλὸν ἀλεξητῆρα μάχης, 20.396) | "warder-off" | "defender" | "protector", "champion"; from ἀλέξω "ward off" (table), with ἐσθλός "good" |
| ὑπὲρ μοῖραν (μὴ καὶ ὑπὲρ μοῖραν δόμον Ἄϊδος εἰσαφίκηαι, 20.336) | "beyond fate" | "beyond what is fated" | "beyond portion" and "beyond what was allotted" (the Odyssey's ὑπὲρ μόρον, a different word), "beyond his share", "against fate"; μοῖρα "fate" as in the table's μοῖραν … πεφυγμένον ἔμμεναι (6.488) |
| χαλκοπαρῄου (κυνέης διὰ χαλκοπαρῄου, 20.397; two-ending adjective, "of the bronze cheek-pieces") | "bronze-cheeked" | "bronze-cheeked" | "bronze-faced", "with bronze cheek-guards", "bronze-plated"; χαλκός "bronze" + παρειά "cheek"; the helmet is κυνέη "helmet" (table) |
| ἐρρέτω (20.349, a one-word unit; imperative of ἔρρω) | "Let him go his way with ill luck" | "Let him go, and ill luck go with him" | "Let him go to ruin", "Let him be gone", "to perdition", "be damned" (each says he is doomed, which the verb does not; the table's ἔρρω is "go with ill luck", 8.239) |
